acs: parse signature becomes parse(input: string, now: Date, reverted?: Array<{start: number; end: number}>); existing two-arg calls compile unchanged
ParseResult gains displaced: Array<{ start: number; end: number }> listing earlier same-kind token ranges superseded by a later token

parse('pay rent friday monday', now) yields the Monday date, a chip on 'monday', displaced containing the range of 'friday', and title === 'pay rent' — displaced ranges are excluded from the title exactly like chip ranges
Last-wins applies per kind to date, time, list, priority, and recurrence independently
Displacement compares pre-merge tokens: parse('dinner tomorrow 3pm 4pm', now) keeps the date, time becomes '16:00', and displaced contains only the '3pm' range

Tokens inside reverted ranges are never matched: with reverted covering 'tomorrow' in 'Email #invoices tomorrow friday', the result has the Friday date, displaced is empty, and 'tomorrow' remains in the title
FR-9 of tasks/prd-command-bar-todo.md (first-wins) is explicitly superseded; every existing first-wins test in src/lib/parser.test.ts is rewritten to assert last-wins + displacement
Date-anchor ambiguity tests ('Pay May invoice' stays literal) still pass unchanged
All non-duplicate-token grammar tests (anchored dates, yesterday/today/tomorrow, times, #list <=32 word chars, !p1-!p3, recurrence forms) pass unmodified — FR-105 invariance

token_precedence.value: pass order recurrence->date->time->list->priority; LAST-wins per kind (supersedes first-wins / old FR-9); earlier same-kind token ranges reported in ParseResult.displaced; chip AND displaced ranges are both excluded from title; tokens inside reverted ranges match nothing

sealing.value: displaced text is removed from the field only when the displacing token is sealed (followed by whitespace, or on submit); until sealed it renders demoted; seam collapses to a single space; live field is never trimmed

serializer_token_order.value: title, date, time, recurrence, list, priority

date_serialization.value: yesterday/today/tomorrow at now-1/now/now+1; '<mon> <day>' within next 12 months; '<mon> <day> <year>' otherwise; chip display shows year when date year != now year

esc_two_tier.value: Esc reverts the most recent session chip ((kind, parsed value) absent from mount-time baseline parse); with no session chips Esc invokes onCancel (edit: cancel; bar: existing behavior)

chip_class.notes: class name intentionally unchanged when chip CSS moves to ParsedInput.css in US-104, keeping the visual baseline stable
